sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Iqta System**: A unique land-grant mechanism where the **Iqtadar** (or Muqti) collected revenue from a territory to maintain troops and remit the surplus (**Fawazil**) to the central treasury.
• **Agrarian Taxation**: The state claimed a share of produce, primarily **Kharaj** (tax on non-Muslims) and **Ushr** (tax on Muslim land), with **Alauddin Khalji** being the first to measure land (**Paimaish**) for tax assessment.
• **Market Regulations**: The **Diwan-i-Riyasat** was established to control prices, supply chains, and market inspectors (**Shahna-i-Mandi**) to ensure military sustainability.
• **Key Metric**: The **Hasil** (actual revenue collected) vs. **Jama** (estimated revenue) determined the fiscal health of the Sultanate.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Fixed prices for all commodities; direct state collection; abolition of middleman (Khuts/Muqaddams).
Need to maintain a massive standing army against Mongol invasions.

Mains: Analysis of 'failed' vs 'visionary' economic policies.
Abolition of 24 taxes (Abwabs); Introduction of 'Haq-i-Sharb' (Irrigation tax); Canal construction.
Focus on welfare state and agrarian stability to appease the nobility.

Department of Agriculture established by MBT to bring uncultivated land under the plough.
Cesses or extra taxes levied over and above the standard land revenue, abolished by FST.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Monetary Policy**: Introduction of the **Tanka** (Silver) and **Jital** (Copper) by Iltutmish, standardizing the currency system.
• **Agrarian Expansion**: The state provided **Sondhar** (agricultural loans) to farmers to encourage cultivation in the Doab.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Corruption in the Iqta system, over-taxation leading to peasant revolts, and the failure of token currency due to lack of state monopoly on minting.
• **Solutions**: Centralization of revenue collection and investment in irrigation infrastructure.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'A-M-F' (Alauddin, Muhammad, Firoz).
• **Decoded Meaning**: A (Alauddin = Market/Price Control), M (Muhammad = Token Currency/Agriculture), F (Firoz = Irrigation/Tax Reform).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Diwan-i-Mustakhraj' (Revenue arrears) with 'Diwan-i-Kohi' (Agriculture). Remember: Mustakhraj = Must-collect (arrears); Kohi = Kheti (Agriculture).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Fiscal Centralization' to describe the shift from the decentralized Iqta system to the more direct control seen under the Khaljis.

keyTakeaways: The Delhi Sultanate economy was primarily agrarian, with the state acting as the supreme landlord.
Alauddin Khalji's market reforms were the first instance of state-led price control in Indian history.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq's focus on irrigation (canals) laid the foundation for long-term agrarian productivity.
